enhancement.detailedExplanation:
India Code rule: Sections 37–45 regulate performance of contractual promises, refusal to accept performance, refusal to perform wholly, performance by the promisor or authorised substitute, joint liabilities and joint rights.

Definition: These provisions determine how contractual promises are to be performed and how obligations and rights devolve where several promisors or promisees are involved.

Ingredients:
1. Identify the promise and the party bound to perform.
2. Test whether performance has been offered and properly refused.
3. Apply sections 40–41 where personal performance or third-party performance is relevant.
4. For joint promisors, apply the statutory rules on contribution, release and discharge.
5. For joint promisees, identify the statutory devolution of rights.
examples: A, B and C jointly promise to pay D. D may proceed against any one joint promisor according to section 43, subject to the statutory rights of contribution among the promisors.
problemApplication: Apply sections 37–45 to a factual problem by identifying the statutory trigger, testing every ingredient, checking exceptions or limitations, and stating the legal consequence.
keyTakeaways: Sections 37–45 regulate performance of contractual promises, refusal to accept performance, refusal to perform wholly, performance by the promisor or authorised substitute, joint liabilities and joint rights.
